families.rationale: Lakonishok and Lee's net purchase ratio: issuers whose insiders are net buyers over six months outperform (Lakonishok and Lee, 2001; Jeng, Metrick and Zeckhauser, 2003).
Among names with an insider purchase this quarter, the largest buying relative to the name's own turnover; names without a purchase have no score (NaN, ineligible).
Non-routine (opportunistic) purchases carry the information (Cohen, Malloy and Pomorski, 2012); routine buyers are excluded by the same-month-of-the-prior-year rule.
Purchases by two or more insiders in one quarter are the strongest (Alldredge and Blank, 2019); a name without a cluster has no score.
The most recently filed purchase first: the information is freshest the day it is filed.
Buying relative to turnover, only where a purchase was filed within the last ten sessions.
Contrarian purchases after a decline are the profitable ones (Jeng, Metrick and Zeckhauser, 2003); only names with a negative twenty-session return are scored.
The declared weak prior: among names with insider sales, the lightest relative to turnover (sales are mostly liquidity-driven and uninformative, and most recent sales are plan trades).

rationale: A predeclared fixed set of eight insider-trading formulas, one hypothesis each, scored once without search on daily bars read at D-1 together with the six dimensionless insider_fields_v1 columns (insider_net_ratio, insider_buy_rel, insider_sell_rel, insider_buyers, insider_buy_age, insider_opp_buy_rel), so search-power check B does not apply; checks A and C still bind. The source is the SEC's Insider Transactions Data Sets (quarterly Form 3/4/5 archives); only original Form 4 non-derivative open-market purchases (code P) and sales (code S) by officers and directors count. Visibility is the EDGAR filing date, not the trade date: a filing dated F is public by 17:30 ET on F, so a field holding state at T is first read by decision session T+1 at 10:35 ET with at least 17 hours of slack, and a filing dated on a non-session is visible from the next session. Rule 10b5-1 plan trades are kept in v1 (exclude_10b5_1 is false) because the AFF10B5ONE flag only exists in filings from April 2023, so excluding them would change the sell-side fields' meaning mid-sample; about four in five recent cohort-v2 sales are plan trades, which is why sales are treated as the weaker side, and a second look may flip it. Cohort symbols map to issuer CIKs through the SEC's company_tickers.json; a covered name with no activity in a window holds a real zero, a name never covered by any qualifying filing is NaN, and a name change that moves a ticker onto or off a cohort symbol is an identity break (fields NaN before the latest break). Trades above 10 times the filing session's 20-session median dollar volume are dropped as entry errors. The inputs are the digest-pinned acquisition of the SEC archives and ticker map and the corporate-actions acquisition. The seven conditional formulas divide by their 0/1 condition, so an out-of-condition name has no score (NaN, ineligible) and each session's decile is taken among in-condition names only. The population is cohort v3, the mid-liquidity band of ranks 401-1,400, with the absolute $5 million 20-session median dollar-volume floor and a 15 bp decisive cost; survivorship caveat as for cohort3-events-v1. The cohort, label cube, windows, selection, gates, bootstrap, power and null-check parameters are the matching short-volume protocol's, so the cached cube is reused and the lane-wide confirmation window remains unused until a finalist freezes; the campaign runs only on operator approval. The filings start in 2015, before the bar window, so every discovery block carries an insider score and the discovery gate's 3 of 4 positive blocks binds as written.
title: Insider pooled campaign v1 on cohort v3 (mid-liquidity band, ranks 401-1,400): daily bars read at D-1 plus the six insider_fields_v1 SEC Form 4 insider-trading fields, predeclared fixed set of eight formulas (checks A and C), one-shot lane-wide confirmation
